why: These figures look correct for 2026-27 but are typed literals, although the file header says no figure is typed here. They will go stale silently if the rates change.

claim: Motor vehicle and accommodation allowances are exempt up to 88 cents a kilometre and $328.85 a night in 2026-27.

claim: Payslip line paid 'at a multiple of your base rate such as 2.25 or 2.5 times'

They match 225%/250% today, but they will go stale without warning if the award data changes. The same applies to the typed '25% casual loading' (lines 155, 218) and the Nurses Award 'extra 50%' (line 156).

claim: pre-16 August 1978 service is taxed at a flat 5%, while post-1978 service is taxed at 32% (up to the whole-of-income cap)
why: ATO rules: for pre-16 Aug 1978 service, 5% of the amount is included in assessable income and taxed at marginal rates, so it is not a flat 5% tax. 16 Aug 1978 to 17 Aug 1993 service is taxed at a maximum 32%. Post-17 Aug 1993 service is taxed at marginal rates unless the termination is a genuine redundancy. The whole-of-income cap applies to ETPs, not to unused long service leave.

claim: usually $1,119.10 a week (for 2026-27) ... less than $26.44 an hour. Many employers pay more, and enterprise agreements often do.
why: $1,119.10 is typed into the prose instead of using STANDARD_WEEKLY_RATE, and $26.44 is typed instead of coming from the minimum-wage constant, so both will drift on the next wage review. 'Many employers pay more, and enterprise agreements often do' is a claim about how many employers do this, with no figure or source.

claim: Long service leave ... Calculated at 8.67 weeks per 10 years of service on a pro-rata basis. (The methodology at line 73 uses the same formula.)
why: 8.67 weeks per 10 years matches NSW, Vic, Qld, WA and Tas. SA and NT give 13 weeks after 10 years, and the ACT uses a different accrual. The text presents one rate as national.

claim: Hardcoded '15%' contributions tax, '45%' top marginal rate and '12% of OTE' (lines 118, 123, 124, 132, 141)

claim: No replacement agreement was listed by the Tasmanian Industrial Commission when we checked on 24 September 2026, so the 1 December 2025 salaries remain the latest published rates.
why: The agreement ended on 30 June 2026 and was last checked on 24 September 2026. The TIC list needs a fresh check before this page is relied on, because a replacement agreement could bring back-dated rates. The FAQ answer at line 122 has the same claim.

why: Optional super is not a tax obligation. 'Recommended' is an unlabelled opinion. The SG is calculated on ordinary time earnings, not on assessable income.

The employer's deadline is 14 days: if it has no declaration by then, it lodges one with the details it has. This sentence applies the 28 days to the whole declaration. Line 180 ('If you don't provide your TFN within 28 days') also suggests the 47% rate starts only after 28 days, even when you have

why: The ATO test is GST turnover of $75,000 or more, not more than $75,000. GST turnover also counts all business income, not only delivery work. GST_THRESHOLD is hard-coded at line 10 and not held in lib/constants.

why: These figures are typed into the prose but already exist as constants (also lines 150, 328, 437). They will fall out of step with the constants at the next update.

claim: Is a working holiday maker a non-resident? Not for tax purposes... Standard non-resident rates only apply if the employer has not registered as an employer of working holiday makers.
why: A WHM can be a resident or a non-resident for tax, and WHM rates apply either way. An unregistered employer changes only the withholding rate, because the income is still assessed at WHM rates. The figure also comes from WHM_TAX_BRACKETS_2025_26 while the page is labelled FY2026-27.

why: The employer pays SG on top of ordinary time earnings. It is not taken out of the employee's gross pay unless the salary is quoted as a package. The 12% is also typed in, not taken from the SG constant.

claim: Any pre-tax salary sacrifice to superannuation reduces your gross employment income reported to Centrelink, potentially keeping your payment higher.
why: This contradicts the page's own FAQ (centrelink-income-test-faqs.ts line 51: Centrelink adds salary-sacrificed amounts back to income) and step 3 on line 197 (report pay before salary sacrifice deductions). Services Australia counts salary-sacrificed amounts as income.

claim: Minimum shift: 1 hour for a lone cleaner at a stand-alone site of up to 300 square metres, 2 hours up to 2,000 square metres, 3 hours from 2,000 to 5,000, and 4 hours at 5,000 square metres or more (cl 13.5(c)).

claim: A non-resident receiving dividends from an Australian company typically faces a withholding rate of 15% under most DTAs, reduced from the standard 30% domestic rate.

claim: There is no concessional tax treatment for leave loading, whether it is paid while you take leave or paid out on termination.
why: Leave loading paid out with unused annual leave in a genuine redundancy, or accrued before 18 Aug 1993, follows the same capped (30% plus Medicare levy) treatment as the leave itself. Same issue on line 292 ('taxed at marginal rates, not at a flat rate').

claim: PAYG instalments threshold to enter: tax liability of $1,000+
why: This is a locked table cell and it is incomplete. For individuals, the ATO entry test also needs instalment income of $4,000 or more, and notional tax must be $1,000 or more.

why: The $22.04 figure is typed into the prose instead of coming from code. The same is true of $1,119.10 (line 521) and the $41.41 industry allowance (lines 534 and 538). If those values change at the next Annual Wage Review, the prose will go stale and stop matching the computed rates.

claim: SA: 'Before 10 years the pro-rata payment is not payable if you are dismissed for serious and wilful misconduct ...'

claim: answer Yes only if total income from all sources will be less than the threshold
why: Boundary is inconsistent across the page: line 156 says 'less than the threshold', while line 175 and the FAQ answers (tax-free-threshold-faqs.ts lines 29 and 33) say '{T} or less'. One wording should be checked against the ATO TFN declaration and multiple-jobs pages and used everywhere.

claim: Employer-paid health insurance is a Type 1 benefit.

claim: A TOIL day is 'often shown as its own line with a running balance' on your payslip.
why: This is a claim about how often payslips show TOIL, and the page gives no source for it. Payslip rules (Fair Work Regulations reg 3.46) do not require a TOIL balance line. Either cite a source or reword it as a check the reader can make.

claim: Work Bonus: the first $300 of employment income each fortnight ... the 100-hour work rule.

claim: earnings for the $190,100 high income threshold
why: The figure is correct today and matches HIGH_INCOME_THRESHOLD.current. claim: HECS-HELP repayments: RFBA counts toward the $69,528 marginal-system threshold

why: Hard-coded award figure. Check whether it reflects the 1 July 2026 increase. It should come from the data file.

claim: All employees (salaried, hourly permanent and hourly casual) receive the SG from their employer, and there is no minimum earnings threshold.
why: Employees under 18 who work 30 hours or less a week are not entitled to SG (and private or domestic workers have a similar hours rule). 'All employees' is too wide.

why: This is a typed rate, not taken from a constant. It should come from a TAX_BRACKETS_2027_28 constant.

claim: Super contributions directly reduce the income tax you pay today through concessional tax treatment ... compared to marginal rates of 30%, 37%, or 45% outside super.
why: Employer SG does not reduce your income tax, and non-concessional contributions get no tax break. Only salary sacrifice and deductible personal contributions do. why: The claim is too broad. Employees under 18, and private or domestic workers, are only eligible when they work more than 30 hours in a week.

claim: You need a TFN before starting work.
why: This contradicts the FAQ at first-job-pay-guide-faqs.ts line 24 ("You can start work before receiving your TFN. You have 28 days to provide it") and the page's own next paragraph (line 61). One of the two statements has to go.

claim: Casuals get the 25% loading instead of paid leave, so there is no paid public holiday and no long service leave accrual shown. In {stateName}, check whether your state long service leave law covers casuals
why: The site's own long service leave hub FAQ (long-service-leave-faqs.ts line 68) says casuals are covered in every state and territory where service is continuous. why: The percentages match apprentice-electrician.ts but are typed into the prose rather than rendered from it, so they will drift. The 'many employers' population claim has no source.

claim: Minjilang|A
why: Minjilang is the community on Croker Island, which is listed as AS (line 108). The two codes disagree, and a remote island community is more likely to be the special area. Check against the ATO NT list.

claim: a Medicare Levy Surcharge of 1 to 1.5% applies above ${formatAUD(MEDICARE_LEVY.surcharge.tier1.min - 1)} if you do not hold private hospital cover
why: The 1% and 1.5% rates are typed literals, but the file header says every figure on this page comes from the engine. The threshold shown is the singles tier 1 figure only. Family thresholds are higher, so the sentence states the singles threshold as if it applied to everyone.

claim: Since 1 July 2022, all employees, including casuals, are entitled to SG regardless of how much they earn
why: Removing the $450 threshold did not remove the under-18 rule: employees under 18 who work 30 hours or less a week are still not entitled to SG, and the same 30-hour rule applies to private or domestic workers. As written, 'all employees' overstates who is covered.

claim: The same pro-rata principle applies to personal/carer's leave, compassionate leave, and long-service leave.
why: Under the NES, compassionate leave is 2 days per occasion for every employee (part-time employees get the full 2 days paid). It is not pro rata.

claim: Even backpackers from the 11 reciprocal countries do not pay the Medicare levy; the exemption applies to all WHMs regardless of country of origin.
why: Foreign-resident WHMs pay no levy, but a WHM who is an Australian tax resident needs a Medicare levy exemption (not entitled to Medicare benefits). claim: Superannuation at 12% adds another ...

claim: Student Police Officers are paid $1,360 per week for Session 2, an arrangement introduced "from March 2024".
why: The rate dates from March 2024 and the award has since given rises of 4% (2024), 4% (2025) and 5% (2026). The page already marks it as undated, but it is probably stale and should be checked again against the NSW Police recruitment page.

claim: NSW Health pays interns $80,638 a year from the first full pay period on or after 1 July 2025 (IB2026_007, an interim increase pending the NSW Industrial Relations Commission's decision).
why: This is an interim rate from a bulletin dated 20 January 2026 and backdated to 1 July 2025. By late October 2026 the NSW IRC decision or a 2026-27 rise has probably replaced it. The figure is also hard-coded as 80_638 in the JSX and not held in a data constant.

claim: $18,200 tax-free threshold (also typed at lines 120, 130, 162, 172, 182)
why: $18,200 is typed by hand on this page, but the FAQ file reads TAX_FREE_THRESHOLD. The bracket rows at lines 130-132 ($45,000, $135,000, 30 cents, $27,000) are also typed by hand and could drift from TAX_BRACKETS.

claim: JobSeeker for a single principal carer of a child under 16 has the same 40-cent taper over ${formatAUD(150)} a fortnight
why: $150, the 40-cent taper and the under-16 age are typed into the FAQ rather than read from constants (the constants file comment at line 16 holds the allowance free area $150/$256).

claim: Leave provisions (annual leave at 7.69%, personal leave at 3.85%) are added on top of base salary as on-costs, and the worked example (lines 325-326, 335) adds them to the $95,000 salary to reach the total cost.
why: For a salaried employee, paid annual and personal leave is already paid out of the base salary. Adding the leave provisions on top counts that leave twice, unless the page says these are the cost of backfilling the role while the employee is on leave. The line 335 claim that the gap to take-home pay is partly 'made up of ... leave provisions' has the same problem. This is a methodology question fo

claim: Superannuation row: Employee $10,944 (employer-paid), on $91,200
why: The figure is hand-typed in a table cell beside a formatPercent(SUPER_GUARANTEE.rate) header. 12% of $91,200 is $10,944, so it is correct today but goes stale if the rate changes. It should be derived from SUPER_GUARANTEE.rate.

claim: Under the 2025-26 thresholds (the latest the ATO has published) ...
why: The page runs on FY2026-27 rates and still quotes 2025-26 Medicare low-income thresholds. Check whether the 2026-27 thresholds are out yet.

claim: Repayments use the marginal model ...: 15 cents per dollar over the threshold rather than a percentage of total income.
why: This is incomplete. Under the 2025-26 marginal model, a higher rate applies above the upper band, so '15 cents per dollar over the threshold' is true only for the first band.

claim: Super is payable on casual earnings at the SG rate regardless of hours worked.
why: The $450 monthly threshold is gone, but employees under 18 are only owed SG if they work more than 30 hours in a week. So 'regardless of hours worked' is wrong for under-18 casuals.

claim: A Correctional Officer Trainee is paid $65,146 a year ... from the first full pay period on or after 1 December 2025 (Annex A).
why: Every other ACT figure, ratesEffectiveFrom and the Annex A column heading ('1% + $1,000 from 4/12/2025') date the rates from 4 December 2025. The trainee line says 1 December 2025. One of the two dates is likely a transcription slip.

claim: Annual leave payouts are taxed as ordinary income at your marginal tax rate.
why: This leaves out the ATO rule that unused annual leave (and loading) paid on genuine redundancy, invalidity or early retirement is withheld at a flat 32%, as are pre-18 Aug 1993 amounts. The LSL calculator on the site already models the equivalent rule for LSL.

claim: SG on commission applies 'up to the quarterly maximum contribution base'.
why: Payday Super starts on 1 July 2026. My understanding is that it turns the maximum contribution base into an annual amount, so 'quarterly' may be out of date for the 2026-27 page. The FAQ answer at commission-tax-faqs.ts line 54 only says 'maximum contribution base', so the two places do not match.

claim: Moving into a higher bracket ... so a raise always increases take-home pay.
why: The claim is true for brackets but wrong for the Medicare levy surcharge cliff at $105,001 (whole income, no private hospital cover). The answer names the surcharge only as something that makes a raise 'feel small'. The FAQ also feeds FAQPage JSON-LD.

claim: Includes the low income tax offset and the 2% Medicare levy.
why: The 2% Medicare levy rate is typed as a literal rather than formatted from MEDICARE_LEVY.rate.

claim: Sidebar: 'See exactly how much tax you owe under the current FY2025-26 brackets'.
why: Today is 27 Oct 2026, so the current year is FY2026-27 and the 15% second rate applies. The copy is stale. It should take its year from SITE_CONFIG.financialYear.

claim: a single homeowner with {formatAUD(433_000)} of assessable assets is {formatAUD(100_000)} over the limit, so the pension drops by {formatAUD(300)}
why: The example's excess ($100,000) and reduction ($300) are typed literals, not calculated from PENSION_ASSETS_TEST.fullPensionLimit.single.homeowner (333,000) and taperPerThousand.single. They match today. When the limit is indexed on 1 July, the text will drift while assetsTestRate() in the same sentence updates, so the example will contradict itself.

claim: In the meantime, your employer withholds tax at the higher no-TFN rate
why: Under ATO rules, an employee who tells the employer they have applied for a TFN has 28 days before the no-TFN rate applies, and withholding stays at normal rates during that time. This also contradicts the FAQ at line 20 ("If you don't provide a TFN (or tell your employer you have applied for one)").

claim: Every employee now receives superannuation regardless of how little they earn.
why: Too broad. Employees under 18, and private or domestic workers, are still only eligible for SG if they work more than 30 hours a week.

claim: Take-home assumes a resident on the tax-free threshold for 2026-27, private hospital cover, and no HELP debt.
why: The financial year is hard-coded and will go stale at 1 July 2027, while the tax engine follows SITE_CONFIG.financialYear. Also, calculatePayBreakdown is called without includeHECS here (line 85), so check that it defaults to no HELP.

claim: This calculator applies the loading first and then the overtime multiplier, which matches the common approach.
why: This is a population claim with no source. Several major awards (for example Retail and Hospitality) set casual overtime as an additive percentage (such as 175%) rather than compounding 125% x 150%, so 'the common approach' may be wrong.

claim: On JobSeeker, Parenting Payment, Youth Allowance or Austudy it is {formatAUD(250)} to {formatAUD(500)}
why: The range is hard-coded instead of read from the constant. Also, ADVANCE_LIMITS.allowance.label includes ABSTUDY, but this hero sentence leaves ABSTUDY out.

claim: Below the $300 total work-related threshold ... claim up to $150 for laundering eligible work clothing without written records
why: $300 and $150 are typed literals. They belong in a deductions constants file with their ATO source so they cannot drift from the $300 threshold used elsewhere on the site.

claim: every bonus dollar sits in your top bracket (30%, 37% or 45%) plus the Medicare levy
why: The rates are typed into the prose and leave out the lowest taxed bracket (15% for 2026-27). An employee under that bracket's upper limit pays the bonus at the lowest rate, not 30%, 37% or 45%. The list should come from the bracket constants, or the sentence should cover every bracket above the tax-free threshold.

claim: WA Education Assistants and Tasmanian Teacher Assistants are paid for the weeks they work, with recreation leave and public holidays paid on top, unless they choose to annualise.
why: The WA data (notes line 523, FAQ line 547) mentions only the 25% casual loading. It has no clause on term-only pay or on electing to annualise, so the WA half of this claim has no source on the WA page. Only Tasmania has the annualise election (clause 2, line 650). The hub FAQ at line 1006 also describes WA holiday pay differently: it covers casual EAs only.

claim: Carry-forward of unused concessional cap amounts from the previous 5 years if total super balance is under $500,000; LITO up to $700 phasing out $37,500 to $66,667 (line 160); $268 / $5.15 rate-cut figures; NMW $24.95 to $26.44.
why: These figures are not wrong as far as I can tell, but they are typed into the prose instead of coming from constants. That makes them likely to go stale. Note that the $500,000 test applies to the balance at 30 June of the previous year.

claim: This calculator uses {SITE_CONFIG.financialYear} rates and shows the tax on the lump sum.
why: The calculator shows only 'Total Payout (Before Tax)' (line 154), and the methodology disclosure in leave-calculator-content.tsx line 319 says 'Tax on payout is not calculated here'. The hero claim is false. It is outside this unit.

claim: Union and professional association fees are listed as non-work deductions that sit outside the $1,000 cap and stay fully claimable on top.
why: The ATO treats union and professional association fees as work-related deductions. Whether they sit inside or outside the $1,000 instant deduction depends on the enacted rules, so check this against the Act or ATO guidance.

claim: They all share one threshold of {T}, and the marginal system charges only on the income above it.
why: The same file's top band row (line 35) says the top band pays a percentage of TOTAL repayment income, not only the income above the threshold. The hero sentence is wrong for repayment income in the top band.

claim: 18 to 20 year olds ... move five percentage points closer to the adult rate, reaching it in stages by July 2029.
why: No data field, header comment or nextIncrease.detail supports the July 2029 end date. The file records only the 1 December 2026 step (PR813654). Check the phase-in schedule against PR813654 and the FWC decision.

claim: The same bonus taxed at the {TAX_BRACKETS[1]} bracket (if income drops below $45,000)
why: The $45,000 threshold is hard-coded, while the rate next to it comes from TAX_BRACKETS[1].

claim: The Australian tax calculator treats Centrelink payments as assessable income for tax purposes.
why: This is too broad. Family Tax Benefit, Rent Assistance and Carer Allowance are not taxable. Only some payments, such as JobSeeker (line 185), are assessable income. I left it unchanged because 'Australian tax calculator' is a mapped query variant.

claim: Deeming applies ... or if it belongs to your partner and they are 60 or older.
why: This partner condition does not match the usual CSHC grandfathering rule. That rule turns on whether the stream and the card have both been held since before 1 January 2015. Please check it against the DSS Social Security Guide for CSHC deeming of account-based income streams.

claim: ratesEffectiveFrom: "15 July 2026 (the date FRV published them; FRV does not say when they took effect)"
why: The header renders this as "Under the ..., from 15 July 2026 (...), the Recruit Firefighter rate is ...", which reads as an effective date. But unverified[0] (line 93) says "no effective date is given". The two contradict each other. Also, the source comment says the FRV page is marked "Updated 15 July 2026". That is the page's update date, so calling it "the date FRV published them" is an inferen

claim: 55% of the $1,119.10 standard rate ... the $41.22 carpenter tool allowance
why: Both figures are typed in rather than taken from code, although both exist in code: STANDARD_WEEKLY_RATE, and toolAllowance 41.22 in spokes.ts:185. The same applies to $2.03 a day / $9.94 a week at line 44 (the cookery note in index.ts:403), and to $18,200, 15% and $45,000 at line 68 (the tax constants).

claim: A salary sacrifice arrangement cannot reduce cash earnings below the national minimum wage or the award/agreement rate, and the employer must reject or reduce the arrangement
why: No legal basis is cited (Fair Work Act s 324 deductions, or the salary sacrifice clause in the National Minimum Wage Order). The rule about whether sacrificed amounts count toward the minimum is not clear-cut, so this needs checking against the FWO before it is stated as a definite rule.

claim: To match an employee on $91,200, a contractor needs to charge approximately $65–$70/hour
why: This is a hand-typed estimate that is not derived from contractorRateToEquivalentSalary(). It may not agree with the rate-to-salary table further down the page.

claim: Medicare levy low-income thresholds are the 2025-26 figures because the ATO had not published 2026-27 levy thresholds. (Same claim in the medicare-levy.csv description at line 78.)
why: This status claim is tied to a date and will go stale once the ATO publishes 2026-27 thresholds. OPEN_DATA.updatedOn is 5 October 2026, so someone should check that it still holds. Also check that the values in MEDICARE_LEVY (28,011 / 35,013 / 47,238 / 4,338) really are the 2025-26 income-year figures and not another year's.

claim: Performance, Christmas, sign-on and referral bonuses all count as qualifying earnings under Payday Super
why: Sign-on bonuses are not clearly ordinary time earnings or qualifying earnings under ATO guidance (SGR 2009/2 ties OTE to ordinary hours of work). Please confirm before relying on this. The same claim appears again at line 102.

claim: Loan fringe benefit valuation: 'Difference between RBA benchmark rate and rate charged'.
why: The benchmark rate is the ATO statutory (benchmark) interest rate for the FBT year, FBT.benchmarkInterestRate. The ATO sets it from RBA lending data, but it is not an RBA rate.

claim: A youth worker who supervises staff or volunteers, including managing the day-to-day operations of a group of residential facilities for persons with a disability, is at Level 3.
why: This example on the youth worker page comes from the SCHADS Level 3 disability wording. It may be copied from the disability support worker entry, so check the Schedule B Level 3 youth or community services wording.

claim: 2027 holiday list has Christmas Day (observed) Monday 27 December but no entry for Saturday 25 December 2027, and the standfirst (line 14) says 9 state-wide holidays in 2027.
why: The note on the same entry and the weekend-rules paragraph both say WorkSafe Tasmania's rules make both the Saturday and the following Monday holidays when 25 December is a Saturday. If so, Saturday 25 December 2027 is missing from the list and the 2027 count may be 10, not 9. The standfirst count is tested against the data, so both must change together.

claim: The ATO treats commissions, bonuses, incentive payments, and profit-share distributions identically for PAYG withholding purposes. All are supplementary payments subject to Schedule 5 withholding at your marginal tax rate.
why: Schedule 5 covers back payments, commissions, bonuses and similar payments. Profit-share distributions are not obviously in scope, and Schedule 5 does not withhold 'at your marginal tax rate' (it uses the period-slice method and has a cap). Needs a check against the ATO Schedule 5 text.

claim: A casual loading of ${EMPLOYMENT.casualLoading * 100}% is already included in the hourly rate under most Modern Awards.
why: This is a population claim ('most Modern Awards') with no source cited on the page. 'Modern Awards' should also be lower case ('modern awards') to match FWO style.

claim: Phase-in FAQ: "... and nothing [now: no rate] has changed yet." The 19 FAQ at line 554 has the same problem: "Not yet: no award pays a 19-year-old more for length of service today."
why: Both statements go stale on 1 December 2026 (PHASE_IN.start), about five weeks from now. They need a date condition built from PHASE_IN.start/inForce, or a code switch after that date.

claim: combined income test: 25 cents per dollar over the free area, then ${formatAUD(53)} plus 30 cents per dollar over band1End
why: $53 is hard-coded. It is correct today (0.25 x (512 - 300)), but it will drift silently if PT.combined.freeArea or band1End change.

claim: Table header 'Into super after 15%', and line 168 '15% offset' and line 178 'the extra 15%' (also FAQ file line 44 '15% tax offset')
why: These are correct today, but they are literal 15% figures and are not tied to CONTRIBUTIONS_TAX_RATE / DIVISION_293.rate. They will drift if those constants change.

claim: taxed at only 15% inside super instead of your marginal rate
why: 15% is a typed literal (it also appears at line 98 and in the Division 293 answer at line 126), although the file header says figures come from lib/constants. It should come from a super contributions tax constant so it cannot drift.

claim: Most Teacher Assistants are paid for school terms only, so a year's pay is the hourly rate times the hours and weeks actually worked.
why: This is a population claim with no source. It also reads softer than the same page's hoursNote (line 650) and headline, which say Appendix 16 pays school support staff for school terms only (clause 4), with a written option to annualise over 52 weeks. Pick one: state the Appendix 16 rule, or cite where 'most' comes from.

claim: Sole traders with labour income are also eligible, alongside employees, provided the income qualifies as work-related.
why: The instant deduction was announced for employees' work-related expenses on labour income. Sole-trader eligibility is not in the original policy as I know it. Please check the enacted Act and ATO guidance before keeping this.

claim: Full-time pay before tax.
why: The answer box also shows the ATO average taxable income, which covers every taxpayer with that occupation code, part-time included. Labelling the whole box as full-time pay overstates that row.

claim: H2 'The 47% Withholding Limit'
why: The heading types 47% but all the body text uses SCHEDULE_5_WITHHOLDING_LIMIT. If the constant changes, the heading goes out of date. The heading is locked in this pass.

claim: The National Minimum Wage rose 4.75% on 1 July 2026 to {aud(nmw.weekly, 2)} a week.
why: 4.75% is the modern award increase. The site's own data says the NMW rose about 6.0%: NMW_HISTORY_RAW has 2026-27 published "6.0%", and EMPLOYMENT.minimumWageWeekly 1004.90 / minimumWageWeeklyPrevious 948.00 = +6.0%. The brief also gives the NMW rise as 5.97%. The percentage is typed into the prose, not read from code.

claim: The new lead-in says retail and hospitality workers have these rights under the Fair Work Act and the General Retail Industry Award or the Hospitality Industry (General) Award.
why: Restaurant and many cafe workers are covered by the Restaurant Industry Award (MA000119), and fast food and club workers by other awards, not MA000009. The rights list (2-hour casual minimum engagement, break table) quotes MA000009 clauses that do not apply to them. Resolve this together with the writer's line 80 coverage question.

claim: 2.923 hours of leave per week, or approximately 0.833 days per fortnight
why: 152 hours / 26 fortnights = 5.85 hours = 0.769 days of 7.6 hours per fortnight, not 0.833. 0.833 days would be about 20 days over 24 periods (half-monthly).

claim: Medicare levy low-income threshold labelled '2025-26 threshold, the latest published' on a FY2026-27 page
why: This is stale-prone. Check whether the 2026-27 low-income threshold has now been legislated or announced.

claim: Under most awards the first 2-3 overtime hours are paid at 1.5×, and hours beyond that at 2.0×.
why: Population claim ('typically' in the original) with no cited source. Kept as written, but it should be sourced or tied to named awards.

claim: Tasmania's payroll tax starts at 4% (6.1% once an employer's Australian wages pass $2 million)
why: The rates and the $2 million tier are typed into prose rather than drawn from the payroll-tax constants. The figures match PAYROLL_TAX_STATES.tas.rateSummary today, but they will drift if the constant changes.

claim: Full-time employees who don't work on the public holiday are entitled to their ordinary pay for the day.
why: Under the NES (Fair Work Act s116), part-time employees whose ordinary day falls on the public holiday are paid too. Naming only full-time employees understates who is covered.

claim: ... and {A.maxFortnightly.age13to19} for a teenager
why: Not precise enough. The 13-19 rate applies to a child aged 13 to 15, or 16 to 19 in full-time secondary study. A 16 to 19 year old who is not studying gets nothing. I did not edit this string because the ages would be new numbers in it.

claim: The long-term rate applies after 26 of the last 39 weeks on a non-student income support payment, with no dependent child, starting study or an apprenticeship after turning 22 (21 for Austudy).
why: Austudy is only for people aged 25 and over, so an age condition of '21 for Austudy' looks wrong or garbled. Check the long-term income support student rate conditions against Services Australia.

claim: The right to request part-time after parental leave 'extends until the child reaches school age (or 18 for a child with a disability)'.
why: The 'under 18 with a disability' limit is the old s65 wording, from before the 2013 amendments. Current s65 covers a parent or carer of a child of school age or younger, and a separate carer category covers a child with disability. The 18 cut-off looks out of date.

claim: Worked example Step 5: the employee's RFBA on the income statement is $10,401, the Type 1 grossed-up amount.
why: Reportable fringe benefits amounts are always grossed up at the Type 2 rate. The constants file says the same: 'grossUpType2 ... also used for ALL reportable amounts'. On a $5,000 taxable value the RFBA would be $5,000 x 1.8868 = $9,434, not $10,401.

claim: Overtime hours generally still do not attract superannuation
why: This is a hedge already in the text on a rule. Under the ordinary time earnings rules, overtime is excluded from SG unless an award or agreement says otherwise, so 'generally' should become that stated condition. It was not added in this pass.

claim: Annual leave does not accrue during ... community service leave (except jury duty)
why: Under Fair Work Act s22(3), community service leave counts as service even when unpaid, so annual leave accrues during all community service leave (jury duty and voluntary emergency management), not only jury duty. The FAQ in annual-leave-guide-faqs.ts line 39 only names jury duty, so check that too.

claim: Superannuation Calculator card: 'Calculate employer SG contributions at 12%' and Overtime card: 'penalty rates at 1.5x and 2x ... beyond 38 hours per week'
why: These are locked link-card descriptions. The SG rate is typed by hand rather than taken from SG_PCT, and the card calls overtime 'penalty rates', the same terminology problem as line 437.

claim: Workers with unused cap space from previous years (where their super balance was below $500,000 on 30 June) can carry forward up to 5 years of unused amounts.
why: The $500,000 total super balance threshold and the 5 years are hard-coded rather than taken from SUPER_GUARANTEE. The ATO wording is 'total superannuation balance' on 30 June of the previous financial year, which is more precise than 'super balance ... on 30 June'.

claim: Footnote: 'Most Tasmanian private-sector workers work it [Easter Tuesday] at ordinary rates unless their award or agreement says otherwise.'
why: This is a population claim ('most') with no figure, and the page cites no source for it. The same footnote also says 'generally only for the Tasmanian Public Service', which is a hedge. It needs a Business Tasmania or WorkSafe Tasmania source, or a rewording.

claim: In Victoria, WA and South Australia a plain resignation past 7 years pays out the accrued balance. In NSW, Queensland, Tasmania and the NT a plain resignation pays nothing until you reach 10 years.
why: The ACT is in neither list. Its proRataUnconditionalFromYears is 7, so the table directly below shows an ACT resignation at 8 years as paid. The prose should probably list the ACT with Vic, WA and SA.

claim: Overtime is calculated at 1.5x the base hourly rate for the first 2 hours per day, consistent with most modern awards.
why: This is an unsourced 'most modern awards' claim. Some awards set the first 3 hours at 1.5x (General Retail, for example), and the hourly pros list on line 169 itself says 'first 2-3 hours'. The 12% SG figure is also hard-coded in the prose instead of coming from a constant.

claim: verifiedOn "24 September 2026"; FAQ answer says no determination published "when we checked on 24 September 2026"; notice cites FWC case page "last updated 1 May 2026"
why: VIC was last checked on 24 Sep 2026. WA was re-checked on 22 Oct 2026. The FWC B2023/771 page should be re-read to confirm that no workplace determination has been made since. If one has, the notices and FAQ are stale.

claim: Christmas Day worked when it is not a public holiday is paid 200% (casual 225%).
why: Christmas Day is a national public holiday in every state, so the condition "when it is not a public holiday" reads oddly. Please check cl 6.x of AE531119 to confirm the wording (for example, a substituted day) before the next review.

claim: Medicare Levy component is $1,700 per year ($65.38 per fortnight) on $85,000; SG is $10,200 per year / $392.31 per fortnight (line 310); fortnightly gross $3,269.23 (lines 175, 273, 276).
why: These figures are correct now, but they are typed into the text rather than derived from EX85, MEDICARE_LEVY.rate or SUPER_GUARANTEE.rate. They will go stale if a rate changes.

claim: The higher JobSeeker rate (singleWithChildren) also goes to 'people 55 or older who have been on the payment for 9 months or more, or who have a partial capacity to work'.
why: Services Australia pays this higher rate only to SINGLE people in those groups, and the partial-capacity group is limited to people assessed at 0 to 14 hours. The text does not say 'single' or give the hours band, so a partnered 55+ reader could read it as applying to them. I kept the original scope because adding these facts would mean new figures.

claim: When Anzac Day, Christmas Day or Boxing Day lands on a weekend, the ACT keeps the weekend day and adds a weekday
why: The rule leaves out New Year's Day, but the same page (new-year-2028 section, line ~95) says the ACT lists both Saturday 1 and Monday 3 January 2028. Either the standfirst rule is incomplete or the 2028 section is wrong.

claim: The 12% SG applies to the underpaid amount (also hard-coded at lines 86, 93 and 123)
why: Correction to the writer's line 53: the SG claim is on source line 52. The percentage is typed into the prose rather than taken from SUPER_GUARANTEE.rate, which the FAQ file and the calculator's breakdown row already use.

claim: LITO and the Medicare levy are identical in both years, so the saving is unaffected
why: The Medicare levy low-income thresholds are indexed every year, so the Medicare levy is not necessarily identical in 2025-26 and 2026-27 at low incomes. Check the constants for both years.

claim: these figures do not include the Medicare levy (2%)
why: The 2% Medicare levy rate is typed by hand instead of being read from a constant.

claim: Select 'non-resident' as your residency status in myTax (WHMs are treated as non-residents for tax purposes).
why: Contradicts line 77, which says a WHM can pass the 183-day residency test. Residency in myTax is answered on the residency tests, not visa type; WHM rates apply regardless of residency.

claim: If you work in the Pilbara, the Kimberley or the Goldfields, you may also be entitled to the federal zone tax offset
why: Under ATO rules, zone tax offset eligibility depends on your usual place of residence in the zone (183 days). Fly-in fly-out workers whose usual home is outside the zone have been excluded since 2015, so 'if you work in' overstates who qualifies.

claim: Deputy principals are paid $161,746 to $164,605 and heads of department $145,320 to $155,351.
why: The $145,320 to $155,351 range is the whole Heads of Program (Stream 2) scale. Its top two rows (Level 2, $152,651 and $155,351) are for Senior Guidance Officer and HOSES 3, not Head of Department. Heads of Department alone are Level 1 ($145,320 to $148,003). The label is wider than the figures support. I did not change it.

claim: The super guarantee is calculated on ordinary time earnings.
why: The comment at lib/constants/australian-tax.ts (around lines 130-135) says that from 1 July 2026, under Payday Super, SG is calculated on qualifying earnings rather than ordinary time earnings. The FAQ wording looks out of date.

claim: annual leave (7.6%), personal leave (3.8%) ... 30 to 45% above ... $135,000 to $145,000
why: These are hard-coded. 4 weeks / 52 = 7.69%, which rounds to 7.7%, not 7.6%. 10 days / 260 = 3.85%. The 30 to 45% markup and the insurance and admin cost ranges have no source.

claim: Table cell: 'Tax saving at $100K salary: $1,500 per $10,000 sacrificed'
why: $1,500 is only 30% minus 15%. It leaves out the 2% Medicare levy, so it is $1,700. The /salary-sacrifice-calculator/ hero and FAQ count the Medicare levy in the saving, so the two pages disagree. The figure is also hardcoded.

claim: Clients do not withhold PAYG tax from a contractor's invoices ... unless a voluntary withholding agreement is in place.
why: Clients must also withhold PAYG (no-ABN withholding at the top marginal rate) when a contractor does not quote an ABN, so the only exception named is incomplete.

claim: An employee earning $230,000 with $30,000 concessional contributions ($27,600 SG plus $2,400 salary sacrifice) has a combined income of $260,000 and pays Division 293 tax on $10,000.
why: If $230,000 is gross salary, the $2,400 salary sacrifice comes out of taxable income ($227,600), so Division 293 income plus contributions is $257,600 and the taxed amount is $7,600, not $10,000. SG on OTE also counts sacrificed salary. The example needs to say whether $230,000 is taxable income or gross salary.

claim: Most FIFO employers cover the cost of flights; the travel allowance "is generally taxable unless the employer books and pays for travel directly, in which case it is a fringe benefit to the employer"
why: Most FIFO employers is a population claim with no source. Also, travel the employer books and pays for directly is not an allowance, and FIFO flights are often exempt from FBT under the otherwise-deductible rule. The sentence mixes up two different things.

claim: For a salary of $153,210 or less ...
why: The figure is correct (it matches SALARY_BANDS[1].max), but it is typed into the FAQ answer instead of coming from the constant, so it will go stale when TD 2027 changes the bands. The same typed figure is in travel-allowance.tsx at lines 60, 66, 69 and 102.

claim: NSW Health pays interns $80,638 a year from the first full pay period on or after 1 July 2025, an interim rate that may have been updated.
why: The answer admits the rate may be stale ('may have been updated'), which hedges against its own currency. Confirm the current NSW Health intern rate, put it in the data file and remove the hedge.

claim: The Child Support Agency includes RFBA in adjusted taxable income
why: The Child Support Agency no longer exists under that name. It is now Child Support, part of Services Australia. The page also does not say whether child support counts RFBA in full or at the reduced Centrelink factor used for s57A employers.

claim: Overtime is 'paid at penalty rates of 1.5x (time and a half) or 2.0x (double time)'
